items.title: Mississauga approves 1-year moratorium on AI data centres
items.summary: According to Global News, city council voted to approve a one-year moratorium on artificial intelligence data centres Wednesday. This represents a departure from a pattern that was forming in Ontario. A similar motion for a moratorium was defeated by Hamilton's city council earlier this month. Vaughan has already approved a hyperscale AI data centre, which is nearly finished construction and set to come online in the latter half of this year. Mississauga's motion passed unanimously. Mayor Carolyn Parrish did not cast a vote, as the mayor only votes in case of a tie. The proposal at the centre of Wednesday's vote was a planned 50-100 megawatt site at Tenth Line West and Argentia Road, less than 300 metres from a residential neighbourhood. Both Mississauga and Ontario have been dotted with data centres for years, but, if built, this would be among the province's first hyperscale centres. These types of centres draw significantly more power than smaller sites, presenting more potential issues with noise, water usage and grid capacity. The results of the vote now make it unclear if or how this project will proceed. Speaking to Global News before the vote, city councillor and mayoral candidate Alvin Tedjo said more safeguards are needed, despite data centres' importance to the Canadian economy.

items.title: Is it safe to swim in Mississauga and Brampton? Here's what you need to know
items.summary: According to INsauga and Peel Public Health, residents looking to cool off in the water can head to Mississauga and Brampton beaches with confidence this week, as all four monitored swimming areas are currently safe for swimming. The latest beach water testing results, released Wednesday (July 29), show acceptable bacteria levels at all public beaches monitored across the region. Peel Public Health tests water quality throughout the swimming season to help prevent illness and ensure recreational waters meet safety standards, with testing beginning in June and continuing until the end of the season. The all-clear comes as temperatures rise across the GTA and residents look for ways to beat the summer heat, though health officials continue to remind swimmers that conditions can change quickly, especially after heavy rainfall. High levels of bacteria in beach water can lead to illnesses including diarrhea, skin rashes, ear infections, eye irritation, coughing and congestion. According to Peel Public Health, bacteria levels can increase due to several factors, including heavy rain, stormwater runoff, large numbers of water birds, high winds, wave activity and large numbers of swimmers.

items.title: Temporary freeze put on any new AI data centres in Mississauga
items.summary: According to INsauga, plans to build any major data centres across Mississauga have been temporarily put on hold to allow the city more time to study the matter and any new rules that would regulate the rapidly growing industry. Following some two dozen deputations from residents and other stakeholders at Wednesday's city council meeting, the vast majority of whom spoke against the large new facilities, Mississauga councillors unanimously agreed to impose a moratorium of one year and up to two years on any such developments in the city. The motion tabled by Ward 9 Coun. Martin Reid sought to temporarily halt the development of major data centres in Mississauga, calling for an Interim Control Bylaw that would prohibit new large-scale digital infrastructure facilities including artificial intelligence, cloud computing and hyperscale data centres for up to one year while the city undertakes a comprehensive planning study. The temporary pause agreed to by council applies citywide and can be extended to a second year if additional time is needed to complete the review. Mayor Carolyn Parrish said post-vote that residents' fear of the unknown as it relates to huge data centres and their impact is understandable. Wednesday's discussion, which took up most of the day inside council chamber at city hall, comes after months of growing concern among residents over a proposed Prologis data centre in Meadowvale.

items.title: Wild turkey sits on car, hangs out in Mississauga neighbourhood
items.summary: According to INsauga, a wild turkey is hanging around a Mississauga neighbourhood, sitting on cars and generally making itself at home. A resident named Ricardo photographed the bird standing on top of a parked car and roaming around the neighbourhood, jokingly commenting that it is "protecting us from car theft." Community members first saw the wild turkey in the neighbourhood a few months ago, and it recently returned for what appears to be an extended stay. Residents have seen the bird frequently over the last few weeks, and a community member photographed it sitting on her bench and casually hanging out on a deck. Wild turkeys have become an increasingly common sight in parts of the GTA in recent years as the population has rebounded and birds wander into residential areas in search of food. According to a City of Mississauga spokesperson, Animal Services received three reports of wild turkey sightings in the Hillcrest Avenue and Confederation Parkway area in April 2026.

items.title: Backyard fireworks not allowed over long weekend in Mississauga without a permit
items.summary: According to INsauga and City of Mississauga bylaw enforcement, the Civic Holiday long weekend is just around the corner, but that does not mean Mississauga residents can celebrate with backyard fireworks without first obtaining a permit from the city. While fireworks displays are permitted at people's homes in Mississauga without a permit on Victoria Day, Canada Day, Diwali, Lunar New Year and New Year's Eve, those who want to use the celebratory devices on their property this coming weekend to mark the Aug. 3 Civic Holiday must get prior permission from the municipality. The same permit rules also apply to the next long weekend, Labour Day, which falls in early September. In place of fireworks, City of Mississauga officials have suggested in past years that people celebrate in their backyards with glow sticks, noisemakers or sparklers. As usual on holiday weekends, Mississauga bylaw enforcement officers will be out in full force in the coming days to ensure fireworks are not being sold or used illegally. According to the city, Mississauga residents registered 58 fireworks use complaints with the city's bylaw enforcement department during the most-recent Canada Day holiday period, which ran from June 26 through July 2.

items.title: E-bike rider from Mississauga charged with impaired driving in another Ontario city
items.summary: According to INsauga and Guelph Police, a Mississauga man has been charged with impaired driving after police came across an e-bike rider who had fallen and hurt himself while operating the motorized vehicle on Tuesday night. Investigation revealed the man was riding his e-bike when he lost control and fell over, with the bike falling on top of him, police said in a news release on Wednesday, adding the rider was taken to hospital for treatment. While speaking to the man, the police officer detected an odour of alcohol and noted signs of impairment, police reported. The man was arrested after having failed a roadside breath test, with additional breath samples showing he had more than the legal amount of alcohol in his system, police said. A 40-year-old Mississauga man is charged with impaired driving, and his licence was suspended for 90 days. As use of e-bikes continues to grow across Ontario, police remind those who use the motorized vehicles that they are subject to Highway Traffic Act rules and regulations and must follow the same rules of the road as cyclists.

items.title: Walmart Canada, Associates and Customers Raise $7.2 Million to Support Children's Hospitals Across Canada
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Walmart Canada and its associates and customers have raised $7.2 million to support children's hospital foundations across the country. The funds raised will help provide life-changing equipment, advance groundbreaking research, support specialized training and enhance programs that give children access to the care they need close to home. For more than 32 years, Walmart Canada, its associates and customers have supported Children's Miracle Network, raising and donating more than $250 million since 1994. Every dollar raised stays local, directly supporting children's hospital foundations in communities across Canada. Walmart associates played an important role in bringing the campaign to life and inspiring support in their local communities, rallying behind the campaign in stores and supply chain facilities across the country. Throughout the campaign, patient ambassadors visited Walmart stores across Canada, sharing their personal stories, helping associates and customers see the impact their donations make on real children and families whose lives have been changed because their local children's hospital had the right care, expertise and support when it mattered most.

items.title: Peel Region shelter crisis deepens as intimate partner violence incidents rise
items.summary: According to CBC Toronto, as intimate partner violence incidents rise in Peel Region, local leaders say provincially funded emergency shelters are becoming overburdened and hamstrung by outdated funding rules. The region's shelter system is struggling to accommodate the growing demand, with facilities operating beyond capacity while trying to provide essential services. Mississauga's mayor and the Peel Regional Council have called for increased provincial support and resources to address the crisis. Advocates say the current funding model was designed years ago and fails to account for the complexity of modern cases requiring specialized trauma-informed care and longer-term support. The situation highlights a critical gap between the rising need for safe housing and services for survivors of intimate partner violence and the resources available to support them in the community.

items.title: Mississauga councillor wants pause on AI data centres as Toronto councillors grapple with proposed facilities
items.summary: According to CityNews Toronto, as communities across Canada and the United States deal with a surge in proposed AI data centres, councillors in the Greater Toronto Area say they are trying to push for a more comprehensive response amid environmental concerns. During a meeting of Mississauga city council on Wednesday, Coun. Martin Reid introduced a notice of motion calling for an interim control bylaw to stop the development of "major digital infrastructure facilities" for up to a year so City staff can conduct a planning study as well as a thorough review of bylaws and policies. CityNews met with Reid on Monday at the site of what he said would be the first massive, hyperscale data centre in the community. Located on Tenth Line west of Winston Churchill Boulevard and Highway 401 and near Lisgar GO station, the site is nestled next to a house, a church, greenspace and an existing warehouse. But just hundreds of metres away, there is a large shopping centre along with current and proposed housing subdivisions.

items.title: Child in critical condition after being rescued from pool at Mississauga home
items.summary: According to the Toronto Star and Peel police spokesperson Laurie McCann, a child is in hospital in life-threatening condition after being rescued from a swimming pool in Mississauga on Tuesday morning. Emergency crews responded to a call for a reported drowning, and at the scene, a child was rescued from a residential swimming pool. A spokesperson for Peel Regional Paramedic Service said that a young patient was brought to a local hospital in critical condition following the incident. Peel paramedics provided emergency treatment and transport to the hospital to assist with the emergency response. Police are asking that the privacy of the family be respected during this difficult time. The incident marks another reminder of the importance of water safety and supervision around residential pools.

items.title: Peel Region confirms West Nile virus found in mosquitoes: What you need to know
items.summary: According to Peel Region Public Health and the City of Mississauga, the first West Nile virus case this year has been confirmed in Peel Region. The mosquitoes carrying the virus were identified in Brampton near the intersection of Queen Street East and Kennedy Road North. With the virus now active locally, residents are advised to take steps to protect themselves and their property from infected insects. West Nile virus is a mosquito-borne illness that can cause mild flu-like symptoms in most people, but in rare cases, it can lead to serious illness affecting the brain or nervous system. There is no vaccine or specific treatment for humans, making prevention essential. People more than 50 or with weakened immune systems are at higher risk for serious complications. Mosquitoes that transmit West Nile virus are most active at dusk and dawn. Limit exposure during peak mosquito hours or, if possible, stay indoors during these times. To help prevent the spread of West Nile virus, residents are urged to eliminate standing water on their property, as mosquitoes need only a few millimetres of stagnant water to breed.
